articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot got social-engineered harder than a lonely boomer on Facebook, letting hackers hijack Obama's Instagram with pro-Iranian memes. When the machines become the weakest link, you know we've peaked as a species.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally yeeted AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets onto GitHub like it's their personal dotfiles repo. Congress is demanding answers while we're all just impressed someone finally found a way to make government transparency happen by accident.

articles.title: We're Fighting Mass Surveillance Tech—and Winning
articles.summary: Plot twist: the same CISA contractor who leaked AWS GovCloud credentials also exposed internal CISA systems on a public GitHub repo. Cybersecurity agency gets pwned by basic OPSEC failure—chef's kiss level irony.

articles.title: Zoom CISO: AI as Security Enabler, Not Role-Replacer
articles.summary: Cops are using license plate readers for everything from school residency checks to noise complaints because mission creep is a feature, not a bug. Automated surveillance state speedrun any% world record attempt in progress.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Philly police are literally tracking citizens who criticize AI data centers on social media and calling it 'First Amendment Activity' monitoring. Orwell is spinning in his grave so fast we could power those data centers with his corpse.

articles.title: Claude celebrates Anthropic's stock market float with blockbuster ... outage
articles.summary: Microsoft backed down from threatening zero-day researchers after the security community collectively told them to go touch grass. Rare W for vulnerability hunters who refuse to be intimidated by corporate legal theater.

articles.title: AI-Driven Exploitation is Destroying Vulnerability Management. Here’s How to Handle It.
articles.summary: Oracle WebLogic CVE-2024-21182 got added to CISA's KEV catalog after active exploitation because apparently enterprise software security is still optional in 2025. Oracle gonna Oracle.

articles.title: Anthropic is finally giving the EU access to Mythos, ending weeks of standoff over the world’s most powerful cybersecurity AI
articles.summary: Windows Server vulnerability scores a perfect 9.8 and grants system privileges with a single malformed packet—domain controllers getting rekt in the wild. Microsoft's definition of 'secure by design' continues to be... creative.

articles.title: (2026.06.02) (various)
articles.summary: Anthropic's Mythos AI autonomously discovered 10,000+ zero-days across major operating systems, finally giving EU cybersecurity agency ENISA access after weeks of bureaucratic standoff. When AI becomes better at finding bugs than humans, it's time to update our résumés.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto V cheat service gets hacked, exposing thousands of gamers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: GTA V cheat service promising 'enhanced privacy' got hacked and exposed 64,000 accounts—because nothing says operational security like running illegal game modifications. The irony is so thick you could mine it for cryptocurrency.
